item.title: The country's two largest reservoirs of water are at historic lows
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks with Jack Schmidt, director of the Center for Colorado River Studies at Utah State University, about new record low water levels in two major reservoirs.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks with Jack Schmidt, director of the Center for Colorado River Studies at Utah State University, about new record low water levels in two major reservoirs.

item.title: Trump administration moves to open untouched national forests to logging
item.description: The end of "roadless rule" protections would open millions of acres of pristine forests to commercial use. Supporters say it will lead to better managed forests.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers solicits long-term solutions for Juneau's glacial floods
item.description: This year's glacial outburst flood event in Juneau was minimally damaging, but residents worry about the future. A permanent solution to drain the glacial lake will be chosen by the end of 2026.
item.content:encoded: This year's glacial outburst flood event in Juneau was minimally damaging, but residents worry about the future. A permanent solution to drain the glacial lake will be chosen by the end of 2026.

item.title: A uranium revival brings new worries to tribal lands
item.description: Uranium production has been revived in the US Southwest. Tribal communities there who suffered illnesses from previous development are worried nuclear energy will harm them again.
item.content:encoded: Uranium production has been revived in the US Southwest. Tribal communities there who suffered illnesses from previous development are worried nuclear energy will harm them again.

item.title: States are passing their own clear water laws to counter Trump admin rollbacks
item.description: A 2023 Supreme Court ruling removed Clean Water Act protections for wetlands. The Trump administration is moving to weaken remaining rules. Some states are passing their own clear water laws in response.
item.content:encoded: A 2023 Supreme Court ruling removed Clean Water Act protections for wetlands. The Trump administration is moving to weaken remaining rules. Some states are passing their own clear water laws in response.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Cohen

item.title: EPA issues new rules for controversial herbicide, but opponents worry dangers remain
item.description: Controlling weeds is a perennial problem for farmers. The EPA issued rules earlier this year for one controversial herbicide that can be prone to drifting and harming some other crops and trees.

item.title: Some of the most pristine ecosystems in the U.S. are losing protections
item.description: Some of the most pristine ecosystems in the U.S. are in the Pacific Ocean. They're federally protected, but now, the Trump administration is rolling back some of those protections.
item.content:encoded: Some of the most pristine ecosystems in the U.S. are in the Pacific Ocean. They're federally protected, but now, the Trump administration is rolling back some of those protections.

item.title: The largest human composting facility is coming to Maryland
item.description: The largest human composting facility in the nation is soon opening in Maryland, with capacity to handle 2,000 bodies a year. It's meeting a growing demand for eco-friendly interment options.

item.description: Wildfires in Spokane have destroyed hundreds of homes and led to evacuation orders for 60,000 people.

item.title: What a federal plan to reallocate the Colorado River's water means for western states
item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Russ Schumacher, professor at Colorado State University, about a new government proposal to reallocate water from the Colorado River among Western states who rely on it.
